sample_unit: public breast ultrasound datasets (BUSI, BUS-UCLM, BUS-BRA, BrEaST)

links.outcome: Internal versus cross-dataset AUROC and balanced accuracy with patient-level leakage-aware splitting
links.effect: Cross-dataset testing was weaker than internal testing: mean raw AUROC fell from 0.801 to 0.719 and mean balanced accuracy from 0.723 to 0.635.
links.quote: Cross-dataset testing was weaker on average than internal testing, with mean raw AUROC decreasing from 0.801 to 0.719 and mean balanced accuracy from 0.723 to 0.635.

links.outcome: Performance drop across datasets with different acquisition and curation conditions
links.effect: Mean raw AUROC decreased from 0.801 (internal) to 0.719 (cross-dataset); mean balanced accuracy from 0.723 to 0.635.
links.quote: Cross-dataset testing was weaker on average than internal testing, with mean raw AUROC decreasing from 0.801 to 0.719 and mean balanced accuracy from 0.723 to 0.635.

unlisted_practices: Region-of-interest input cropping to improve external generalization (mean external AUROC 0.666 to 0.805)
Temperature scaling to improve calibration under dataset shift (ECE 0.180 to 0.150; NLL 0.848 to 0.682)

screen.practice: post-hoc calibration (temperature scaling) and ROI input under dataset shift
screen.reason: The study develops a benchmark to evaluate breast ultrasound AI under dataset shift, specifically testing the effects of calibration (temperature scaling) and input preprocessing strategies (ROI vs whole-image) on out-of-distribution performance and calibration error.

primary.practice: post-hoc calibration via temperature scaling and ROI cropping
